reference_sql:
WITH changed_products AS (
  SELECT product_id
  FROM price_history
  GROUP BY product_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)
SELECT SUM(ol.quantity) AS units
FROM order_lines ol
JOIN changed_products cp ON cp.product_id = ol.product_id
alternatives: WITH versions AS (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions FROM price_history GROUP BY product_id) SELECT SUM(ol.quantity) AS units FROM order_lines ol JOIN versions v ON v.product_id = ol.product_id WHERE v.n_versions > 1

WITH product_units AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_lines GROUP BY product_id), changed_products AS (SELECT product_id FROM price_history GROUP BY product_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2) SELECT SUM(u.units) AS units FROM product_units u JOIN changed_products c ON c.product_id = u.product_id

other_way.sql: WITH versions AS (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions FROM price_history GROUP BY product_id) SELECT SUM(ol.quantity) AS units FROM order_lines ol JOIN versions v ON v.product_id = ol.product_id WHERE v.n_versions > 1
other_way.tradeoff: Keeping each product's version count in the step and filtering after the join works, but HAVING keeps the step to the products needed.

FROM order_lines
WHERE product_id IN (
  SELECT product_id FROM price_history GROUP BY product_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)
